business.body: Lloyds Engineering Works Limited (LEWL) designs, engineers, manufactures, fabricates and installs heavy equipment, machinery and engineered systems for process industries — including hydrocarbons, oil & gas, steel, power, nuclear energy and turnkey/LSTK projects — and also trades in metals and metal ores. It has expanded from a specialised heavy-engineering manufacturer into an integrated platform combining engineering, manufacturing, EPC execution, electrical engineering and defence/marine technologies.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Process equipment, packages and LSTK projects:** Heavy equipment, machinery and engineered systems, Pressure vessels, boilers and heat exchangers, Eco pickling plants for the steel industry, Marine loading and unloading arms and loading systems for trucks, tankers and railways, Integrated boiler systems with instrumentation and electrical control solutions
- **Metals trading:** Wholesale of metals and metal ores
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Lloyds Enterprises Limited — holding company: Holding company of Lloyds Engineering Works Limited; does not participate in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives
- Techno Industries Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), acquired October 15, 2024
- Metalfab Hightech Private Limited — subsidiary: Subsidiary company (76.00% held), acquired May 20, 2025
- Lloyds Infrastructure and Construction Limited — associate: Associate company (24.20% held); significant influence by virtue of shareholding and voting; associated since January 30, 2025
- Lloyds Advance Defence Systems Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), incorporated/acquired December 11, 2025, to spearhead a strategic push into the defence sector
- Lloyds Metals and Energy Limited — related party: Sale, purchase, supply and service contracts; common promoter-directors — Mr. Mukesh R. Gupta is Non-Executive Chairman and Promoter-Director of the related party, and Mr. Rajesh R. Gupta is Promoter and Director of the related party
- Trofi Chain Factory Private Limited — related party: Provides food/canteen facility services; Mr. Shreekrishna Gupta, Whole Time Director of the Company, is a Director of the related party
- ICASA Trading Company Private Limited — related party: Provides infrastructure services for availing food/canteen services; common promoters with the Company
- Rajashekhar Mallikarjun Alegavi — related party: Non-Executive Director of the Company providing technical consultancy / advisory services to the Company under a related-party contract
business.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)

business.body:
- Sector diversity across steel, hydrocarbons, infrastructure, defence, marine and power reduces dependence on any single end-market
- Engineering depth across heavy engineering, process equipment and industrial systems
- Integrated delivery — design, engineering, manufacturing and EPC under one platform, offering single-point accountability across the project lifecycle
- Advanced fabrication infrastructure and execution capability
- Long-standing trusted relationships with leading Indian industrial companies
- Strategic location of the Murbad manufacturing hub near a major port and national highway supporting efficient logistics
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Transform from a fabrication-led equipment supplier into an integrated engineering, EPC, infrastructure and technology solutions platform capable of participating across the full project lifecycle.
- Pursue organic plus acquisition-led growth — expanding beyond fabrication into EPC execution, electrical engineering, and advanced/defence engineering through strategic acquisitions.
- Spearhead a strategic push into the defence sector through a dedicated wholly-owned subsidiary (Lloyds Advance Defence Systems Limited), backed by technology tie-ups/MoUs with international partners for drones, naval systems and radar technology.
- Diversify the order book across sectors and customise engineering offerings to client needs, reducing dependence on any single sector or customer.
- Maintain a Net Debt Free balance sheet to underpin the quality and sustainability of growth.
- Enhance existing manufacturing capacities and modernise/overhaul the asset base to build headroom for future growth.
- Build a reputation as a responsible corporate citizen and a track record of long-term stakeholder value creation to strengthen brand value.
- The Board has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy aimed at appropriately rewarding shareholders through dividends and long-term capital appreciation, while striking a balance between dividend payout and profits retained for future needs of the business (which may be used for acquisitions, expansion or diversification). The Company aims to maintain a consistent approach to dividend pay-out over time; for FY2025-26 the Board recommended a final dividend on equity shares.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY2025-26 LEWL expanded capacity and capability primarily through acquisitions rather than greenfield capex: it acquired a 76% stake in Metalfab Hightech Private Limited (a 16-acre fabrication facility in Hingna MIDC, Nagpur, with substantial land availability for future capacity expansion), and moved to acquire the remaining stake in Techno Industries Private Limited (TIPL, electrical engineering — elevators, escalators, motors, pumps) to make it a wholly-owned subsidiary; TIPL has flagged a capex-driven growth plan of roughly Rs. 30 crore over three years to expand capacities across verticals, alongside adding new channel dealers. The Company also incorporated a wholly-owned subsidiary, Lloyds Advance Defence Systems Limited, to build a defence and marine engineering vertical, backed by international technology tie-ups (FlyFocus, Poland — drones; Kliver Polska and Fincantieri, Italy — naval systems; Virtualabs, Italy — radar) rather than owned manufacturing capacity additions. Separately, the Board approved a proposed merger of Lloyds Infrastructure & Construction Limited, Metalfab Hightech and Techno Industries into LEWL to create a unified 'design-to-execution' engineering and infrastructure entity, expected to complete in FY2026-27. The electrical engineering business has set a medium-term aspiration of annual revenues exceeding Rs. 500 crore over the next three to five years, supported by expanded manufacturing investments and market diversification (new geographies including Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Pune, Nashik, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, plus export expansion into the Middle East, Africa and evaluation of the US market).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Customers are increasingly seeking integrated execution partners as project sizes grow, technical complexity intensifies and execution timelines shorten, favouring single-point-accountability engineering platforms like LEWL.
- India's engineering sector is benefiting from accelerated infrastructure development (National Infrastructure Pipeline, Gati Shakti), the 'Make in India' manufacturing push with PLI-linked investment, and defence indigenisation opening new opportunities.
- The Indian capex cycle across industries is visible and expected to support continued order-book growth.
- Healthy order book and growing demand in railways, renewables and industrial sectors are expected to sustain revenue growth following the Metalfab acquisition.
- India's broader macro backdrop — resilient GDP growth, benign inflation and rate cuts — is supportive of continued industrial and infrastructure investment, though global uncertainty (energy prices, subsidy pressures, demand volatility) is flagged as a risk to the environment.
- Order book position grew strongly year-on-year as on 1 April 2026 versus 1 April 2025 (approx. 91% on a consolidated basis and approx. 79% on a standalone basis), providing a promising base to begin FY27.
- Company aspires and plans to execute a major portion of orders in hand within 15 months, barring unforeseen circumstances.
- The order book is well diversified across all sectors, giving the advantage of being balanced and widespread across various industries, with offerings customised to clientele needs.
- Associate company Lloyds Infrastructure and Construction Limited carries a separately reported order book.
